title: Gwilliams et al. 2023 — Introducing MEG-MASC: a high-quality magneto-encephalography dataset for evaluating natural speech processing
description: MEG-MASC provides raw magnetoencephalography recordings from 27 English speakers who listened to about two hours of naturalistic synthesized stories across two sessions. The stories come from the Manually Annotated Sub-Corpus (MASC) and are intermixed with random word lists and comprehension questions. Word and phoneme onsets and offsets are time-stamped in the BIDS events files. The dataset is a benchmark for large-scale encoding and decoding analyses of temporally resolved brain responses to speech.
methods_description: Participants completed two ~1h MEG sessions, listening to four fictional stories in a participant-specific order (five participants completed one session only). Audio was synthesized with macOS text-to-speech using three female voices, speech rates of 145-205 words per minute, and random inter-sentence intervals of 0-1000 ms. Word and phoneme timings were derived by forced alignment with the Gentle aligner and stored in the events files.
